k.description: Distance of the axis x = -k to the left of the y-axis

b.description: Right boundary; its inclusive minimum is the sampled a value plus 1

constraints: Axis of revolution is x = -k, which lies strictly to the left of the interval [a, b]
Radius is r(x) = x - (-k) = x + k > 0 for all x in [a, b]
promptTemplate: Define R as the region bounded above by the graph of f(x) = x and below by the x-axis over the interval [{a}, {b}]. Find the volume of the solid of revolution formed by revolving R around the vertical line x = -{k}.

canonicalSolution.structure: Radius r(x) = x - (-k) = x + {k}. Height h(x) = x. Volume V = \int_{a}^{b} 2\pi (x + k) x dx = 2\pi \int_{a}^{b} (x^2 + k x) dx = 2\pi [x^3/3 + k x^2/2]_{a}^{b}

hints.template: How does shifting the axis of rotation to x = -{k} change the radius of a cylindrical shell at position x?
The radius of a cylindrical shell is the distance from x to the axis of rotation x = -{k}, which is r(x) = x - (-{k}) = x + {k}.
Set up the integral: V = \int_{{a}}^{{b}} 2\pi (x + {k}) x dx = 2\pi \int_{{a}}^{{b}} (x^2 + {k}x) dx.
